subject: 🏃 Saturday — PAL 10K Benchmark Race (Wk 4)
html:
Tomorrow is the San Mateo PAL 10K — but it's a tune-up with a bib, not a clean calibration. The cold changes what this race can tell us. Tuesday's 6×1000m at 6:54 avg / HR capped 166 already gave us a VDOT 54–55 readout — that's our real fitness data point. Tomorrow is about running smart off a virus, collecting whatever signal the body offers, and walking away healthy for the 8-week build ahead.

Race execution (illness-adjusted): Open at 7:25–7:30/mi — deliberately conservative, 10 sec/mi slower than the original plan. HR governor: ≤170 through 5K. At the 5K mark, gut-check breathing, legs, and HR: if all three feel genuinely clean, you can dial toward 7:15 for the back half. If HR is already 165+ or breathing feels labored, hold 7:25–7:30 and cruise home. The all-out finishing kick is cancelled — no sprint to exhaustion, no H10 max-HR capture. A controlled fast finish in the 7:10s is fine; a lung-burning 200m sprint is not. We'll get the clean max-HR read at Presidio on June 21.

Hard abort criteria — non-negotiable: chest tightness, unusual shortness of breath, dizziness, or HR disproportionately high for effort at any point → jog to the side and stop. No heroics. Myocarditis risk is real within days of a viral illness, and no 10K benchmark is worth jeopardizing 8 weeks of training.

Pre-race fuel: Banana + Maurten Drink Mix 160 (40g carbs) 60 min before start. One Maurten Gel 100 at mile 3.5 — same single-gel protocol we tested at B2B. Half LMNT in 14 oz handheld for sodium. H10 strap on and confirmed connected before the start line.

Focus cue: Run the first mile boring. The start-line adrenaline will pull you to 7:00 — resist it. A 7:28 opener that feels easy is worth more than a 7:05 that puts you in oxygen debt with a cold still in your system.

Context: Week 4 of 12, Phase 1 Foundation — 57 days to race day. You've banked 4 weeks of clean training, knee has been 1/5 for 10 straight days, and the VO2 set Tuesday confirmed you're trending VDOT 54–55. The cold is a speed bump, not a setback. Whatever time you run tomorrow is illness-confounded and will not be used for VDOT recalibration or Pivot gate adjustments. Sunday is 6 mi recovery at 9:30+ regardless of how tomorrow goes.

Tonight: Final five-point gate at alarm — no fever 24 hr, above-neck only, RHR within 5 bpm of baseline, energy near-normal, symptoms improving. All five hold → race. Any miss → DNS, no second-guessing. Kit should be staged: Metaspeed Sky Tokyo, H10 strap, bib, Maurten gel, handheld. Bed by 9:30.
